stories.title: Coldcard Hacker Moves $1.6M in Stolen Bitcoin to Ethereum
stories.summary: An attacker behind a theft of funds from Coldcard hardware wallets has started moving the stolen coins. The attacker routed about $1.6 million worth of Bitcoin over to Ethereum. The coins had reportedly sat untouched since the theft.
stories.whyItMatters: Movement of long-dormant stolen funds often signals a cash-out attempt and can give investigators new leads to trace the coins.
whatToWatch: Whether the funds reach an exchange
Further transfers from the same wallets
Any response from investigators or affected users
questions: Who is behind the original Coldcard theft?
Can the funds still be traced or frozen once on Ethereum?

sources.title: Parked Coldcard loot begins moving as attacker routes $1.6M in stolen Bitcoin to Ethereum

stories.title: Japanese Firm Sells Ethereum, Solana, and XRP Gains to Keep $121M Bitcoin Stack
stories.summary: A Japanese company that held Ethereum, Solana, and XRP sold those positions after they turned a profit. It kept the proceeds tied to its Bitcoin holdings, now worth $121 million. The move points to a Bitcoin-focused treasury strategy.
stories.whyItMatters: It's another example of a corporate treasury choosing to concentrate in Bitcoin rather than hold a mixed crypto portfolio.
whatToWatch: Future disclosures on the company's treasury holdings
Whether other firms adopt a similar Bitcoin-only approach
questions: Which company is involved, and what is its stated rationale?
Does it plan to buy more Bitcoin with the proceeds?

sources.title: This Japanese company made money on Ethereum, Solana, and XRP, but sold them anyway to keep its $121 million Bitcoin holdings

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs Rebound as Ether and XRP ETFs End Winning Streaks
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs returned to inflows. At the same time, Ether and XRP ETFs saw their recent runs of daily inflows come to an end. The split suggests a shift in short-term investor demand back toward Bitcoin.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows are one of the clearest signals of institutional appetite across the major crypto assets, and shifts here often precede price moves.
whatToWatch: Next daily ETF flow reports
Whether Ether and XRP ETFs turn to outflows
questions: What drove the rotation back to Bitcoin?
Is this a one-day blip or the start of a trend?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETFs Rebound as Ethereum and XRP ETFs End Winning Streaks

stories.title: CFTC Moves to Dismiss CME's Lawsuit Over Crypto Perpetual Futures
stories.summary: The CFTC filed a motion asking a judge to dismiss a lawsuit that CME brought against it over crypto perpetual futures. The filing sets up a court decision on the regulator's position. Details on the CFTC's specific legal grounds were not given beyond the dismissal request.
stories.whyItMatters: The case's outcome could shape how the CFTC treats perpetual futures, a product type widely traded on offshore crypto exchanges but limited in the US.
whatToWatch: The judge's ruling on the dismissal motion
CME's response to the filing
questions: What is CME's core legal argument against the CFTC?
Would dismissal end the case entirely or allow a refiling?

stories.title: Tether Sued Over Frozen 'Pig Butchering' Funds; 6,600 Students Get Crypto Loans
stories.summary: This roundup covers two Asia-focused crypto items. Tether faces a lawsuit tied to stablecoin funds it froze in connection with a 'pig butchering' scam. Separately, a program provided crypto-backed loans to 6,600 students.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows both the legal exposure stablecoin issuers face over frozen funds and crypto's expanding, if still niche, role in consumer lending.
whatToWatch: Progress of the Tether lawsuit
Outcomes for students under the crypto loan program
questions: Which court is hearing the Tether case, and what does the plaintiff seek?
What terms and risks apply to the student crypto loans?

stories.title: Monad Mainnet Upgrade Cuts Combined Data-Storage Costs by 98%
stories.summary: Monad shipped a mainnet upgrade that makes storing data together on the network far cheaper. The upgrade reportedly cuts these costs by 98%. No further technical detail was given beyond the scale of the savings.
stories.whyItMatters: Lower storage costs could make Monad more attractive to developers building data-heavy applications on the chain.
whatToWatch: Developer adoption following the upgrade
Any change in on-chain activity or fees
questions: Which use cases benefit most from the cheaper storage?
How does the new cost compare with rival high-throughput chains?

sources.title: Monad’s mainnet upgrade makes storing data together 98% cheaper

stories.title: Coldcard Hacker Swaps Stolen Bitcoin for Ether via THORChain
stories.summary: The attacker behind the Coldcard theft used the THORChain cross-chain protocol to swap stolen Bitcoin for Ether. This appears to be the mechanism behind the fund movement now being tracked. The swap moved the coins off the Bitcoin chain entirely.
stories.whyItMatters: Cross-chain swaps like this make stolen funds harder for exchanges and investigators to trace and freeze.
whatToWatch: Further swaps through THORChain or other bridges
Any law enforcement or exchange response
questions: Can THORChain or downstream exchanges flag and block the funds?
Will more of the stolen coins move through the same route?

sources.title: Coldcard hacker swaps stolen Bitcoin for ETH via THORChain

stories.title: Scan Finds 96,000 Fake-Address Outputs Cluttering Bitcoin's UTXO Set
stories.summary: A scan of Bitcoin's unspent transaction output database found roughly 96,000 outputs tied to fake addresses. These entries add clutter to the dataset that every full node must store and track. No proposed fix was detailed.
stories.whyItMatters: UTXO set bloat raises the resource burden on node operators and touches long-running debates about Bitcoin's data efficiency.
whatToWatch: Any developer proposal to address the clutter
Whether further spam-like outputs turn up
questions: Who created these outputs, and for what purpose?
Can they be safely pruned without protocol changes?

sources.title: Scan reveals 96,000 fake-address outputs clogging Bitcoin’s unspent database

stories.title: Mantle Adds Paxos' USDG Stablecoin, Joins Global Dollar Network
stories.summary: The Mantle network integrated Paxos' USDG stablecoin and joined the Global Dollar Network, a group of platforms supporting USDG. The move gives Mantle users another stablecoin option.
stories.whyItMatters: It extends USDG's reach into another network and adds to the growing competition among dollar-backed stablecoins.
whatToWatch: USDG adoption and liquidity growth on Mantle
Other platforms joining the Global Dollar Network
questions: Who else is part of the Global Dollar Network?
How will USDG compete with existing stablecoins on Mantle?

stories.title: Ether and XRP ETF Inflow Streaks End as Bitcoin Funds Rebound
stories.summary: Spot Ether and XRP ETFs saw their recent multi-day inflow streaks stop. At the same time, Bitcoin ETFs rebounded with renewed inflows. The data points to a short-term rotation in investor demand.
stories.whyItMatters: Daily ETF flows remain a key real-time gauge of institutional sentiment toward each major crypto asset.
whatToWatch: Whether Ether and XRP ETFs return to inflows
Continuation of the Bitcoin ETF rebound
questions: What triggered the rotation on this particular day?
Are outflows from Ether and XRP funds a trend or a blip?

stories.title: Bitcoin Reclaims $80K as Dollar Falls Amid Suspected Yen Intervention
stories.summary: Bitcoin climbed back above $80,000 as the US Dollar Index declined. The dollar's drop coincided with suspected ongoing intervention by Japanese authorities to support the yen. The report ties Bitcoin's move to this broader currency backdrop.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows Bitcoin still trades in step with macro currency moves, not just crypto-specific news.
whatToWatch: Further moves in the Dollar Index
Any confirmation of Japanese intervention
Whether Bitcoin holds the $80,000 level
questions: Has Japan officially confirmed intervention?
How much of Bitcoin's move is macro-driven versus crypto-specific demand?

sources.title: Bitcoin reclaims $80K as DXY falls amid continuing suspected yen intervention

stories.title: VARA and Securitize Sign MoU on Tokenization in Dubai
stories.summary: Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority signed a memorandum of understanding with Securitize. The agreement covers cooperation on tokenization innovation in the emirate. No specific projects or timelines were disclosed.
stories.whyItMatters: It signals continued regulatory engagement with real-world-asset tokenization in one of the more active crypto-friendly jurisdictions.
whatToWatch: Any concrete pilot programs or initiatives that follow
Further regulatory guidance from VARA on tokenized assets
questions: What specific projects will result from the MoU?
What is the timeline for implementation?
